rows.speaker: al-Zamakhsharī

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The surah affirms revelation's Divine Source despite disbelief in it and doubts about Resurrection and the Prophet's messengership.
rows.anchor: The sūrah affirms the Divine Source of what has been revealed to the Prophet

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: It highlights natural wonders dependent on God for sustenance; like thunder, they also glorify God.
rows.anchor: all of which are entirely dependent upon God for their subsistence

rows.speaker: author

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Disbelievers who reject God's call and corrupt the earth face worldly calamities and are promised Hell in the next life.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Believers who do right live tranquilly in this world and are promised Paradise in the next.
rows.anchor: those who believe and are righteous live tranquilly in this world

rows.speaker: AF

rows.speaker: M
rows.claim: The things God does not alter for a people are blessings of this life, such as sound health and wealth.
rows.anchor: their blessings related to this life, such as sound health and wealth (M)

rows.speaker: Kl, My, R
rows.claim: Changing what is within a people means misusing God's blessings to disobey Him.
rows.anchor: until they misuse these blessings to disobey God (Kl, My, R)

rows.speaker: some commentators
rows.claim: Some interpret the verse to mean that God changes people's positive or negative circumstances only after they change their own actions and lives.
rows.anchor: Some have also understood God alters not what is in a people until they alter what is in themselves to mean

rows.speaker: Q
rows.claim: God desiring evil for a people means that He wishes to punish them.
rows.anchor: When God desires evil for a people refers to when He wishes to punish them (Q)

rows.speaker: M

rows.speaker: Aj
rows.claim: The communities before it are earlier nations to whom God sent messengers.

rows.speaker: Ṭ

rows.claim: Disbelief in the Compassionate means rejecting God's Oneness, in keeping with the surah's statement that most people do not believe.

rows.speaker: Th
rows.claim: A report links it to Hudaybiyah in 6/628, when a Makkan objected to the treaty's basmala, saying they did not recognize the Compassionate.
rows.anchor: “We do not recognize the Compassionate!” (Th).

rows.speaker: IK
rows.claim: Saying God is my Lord affirms the lordship and divinity of the One whom the disbelievers reject.
rows.anchor: “I believe in and affirm the Lordship and Divinity of the One in Whom you disbelieve” (IK).

rows.speaker: IK
rows.claim: Trusting in God means relying on Him in all affairs.
rows.anchor: In Him do I trust “in all of my affairs”(IK)

rows.speaker: IK
rows.claim: Turning to God means penitently directing oneself to Him, since this right belongs to Him alone.
rows.anchor: In a state of penitence I turn toward Him, for this is His right to which no one else can lay claim

rows.claim: Another interpretation takes the Days of God as punishments inflicted on disbelievers in earlier communities.
